coverage_note: All 31 segments read across 4 partials. Approximately 30% real operating content; 70% boilerplate course scaffolding, UI navigation, and prompt catalog. Doctrine below retains only usable, de-duplicated operating knowledge.
doctrine: Cold email is a predictable input-output system, not a template game. The levers are: infrastructure health, offer quality, signal-based segmentation, and speed-to-lead. Volume is a downstream consequence of getting each lever right. Separate sending infrastructure from primary brand. Reach people whose behavior signals they are ready now, not random prospects who match a demographic. Every artifact produced must be the hardest possible thing for the recipient to say no to.
operating_rules: Offer matters more than copy: no perfect email beats a weak offer; a strong offer survives mediocre copy
Segmentation over volume: break 100k into 20 micro-lists with 20 unique angles rather than one blast
Signal-driven timing beats static lists: social engagement, funding, hiring, news, leadership changes show individual receptivity now
Evergreen beats batch: event-triggered campaign entry (signal match) produces consistent conversion; static list exhaustion does not
Keep emails under 100 words; one singular CTA per email; no multiple directions
Max 4 emails per sequence (opener + 2-3 follow-ups) in a 7-10 day window
Plain text only on first touch: no HTML, images, Calendly links, Loom links, or PDF attachments
Infrastructure decoupling is mandatory: use secondary domains to protect primary brand reputation
Conservative sending per inbox (1-5 emails per inbox per day); multiply via infrastructure scale not per-inbox volume
Warm-up minimum 3 weeks before scaling; enable read emulation on Outlook accounts during warm-up
Verify email list before every send: inbox delivery > volume
Monitor deliverability proactively: flying blind is fatal; SPF/DKIM/DMARC monthly; bounce and complaint rate continuous
Speed-to-lead: reply to positive responses within 30 minutes; this is the single biggest conversion multiplier
Only enrich leads with valid emails to avoid wasting enrichment credits
Sample AI output on small batch before full deployment; override specific rows if quality is unsatisfactory
Strategy before automation: AI cannot fix a weak offer, fuzzy ICP, or messy data
Individual timing signal beats company-level signal: company data (funding, hiring) shows qualification; social signals show receptivity right now
Instruct the Instantly Copilot/AI Sales Agent as your outbound assistant: load business memory (offer, ICP, pain points, writing frameworks) once and standardize all AI outputs across team
Test and iterate on lead searches: no search is perfect on first run; track which leads respond and refine filters

named_methods.name: Coiling the Spring Workflow
named_methods.description: Upfront batch segmentation (job title, department, industry) then template engineering (industry-specific base + name/company swaps) then high-velocity automated sending in dedicated blocks. Eliminates writer's block and SDR burnout.

named_methods.name: Signal Waterfall Construction
named_methods.description: Primary filter (e.g., founded last 2 years), secondary filter (e.g., recently funded), tertiary trigger (social engagement). Write conditional copy variants per cumulative data points. Cap volume at 30 emails per inbox per day.

named_methods.name: Three Profile Monitoring Categories (via Trigify + Instantly)
named_methods.description: Monitor LinkedIn engagement across three profile types: (1) Own Brand posts (warmest; people liking/commenting have demonstrated awareness), (2) Competitor founders/C-suite personal profiles (medium; use topic framing not surveillance language), (3) Thought Leaders whose audience matches ICP (medium-high; mention thought leader in PS as recommendation not as tracking signal). Push engagement signals to Instantly campaign or through Clay for enrichment.
named_methods.metrics: 20-25% positive reply rate reported by Trigify + Instantly users; 1,000+ meetings booked in 6 months (Trigify founder case study, survivorship bias likely)

named_methods.name: Evergreen Campaign Architecture
named_methods.description: Configure lead finder to refresh list continuously. New prospects enter daily when signal matches ICP criteria. Add AI qualification step before campaign entry to filter false positives. No list exhaustion; every entry has a behavioral reason.
named_methods.frequency: Once per campaign type; self-sustaining thereafter

named_methods.name: Sales Brain (Claude Projects + Instantly MCP)
named_methods.description: Claude Project as persistent outbound workspace. Load: pitch deck, ICP definition, case studies, writing frameworks, competitor intel. Build custom skills (cold-copywriting, email-sequence, campaign-analytics, competitor-analysis, subject-line). Connect Instantly MCP to read live campaign data, create sequences, and update campaigns from Claude conversation. Run weekly analytics workflow for optimization.
named_methods.note: Positioning in course feels forward-looking; experimental but described as viable

named_methods.name: Waterfall Email Finding
named_methods.description: Check multiple email providers sequentially (Instantly own finder, then Leadmagic, Prospeo, etc.) until email is found. Maximizes coverage. Coverage varies by seniority: established professionals at large companies have multiple sources; newer employees at small companies are harder to find.

named_methods.name: AI Enrichment Workflow (Instantly native or Clay + GPT)
named_methods.description: Use Instantly AI functions or export to Clay mapped to LLM API (OpenAI, Anthropic, Grok, DeepSeek, Gemini). Generate: fit scores, personalized opening lines, pain point summaries, icebreakers, talking points. Web research agent visits prospect website, LinkedIn, press releases, industry pubs. Prompt pattern: 'Visit this website, extract case studies / recent news / keywords.' Always test output on 100-lead sample before full run.

named_methods.name: Dynamic Segmentation
named_methods.description: Segments that update automatically as lead data changes (engagement status, reply status, company data). Paired with assignment rules (round-robin, territory, custom criteria) for team routing. Archive thoroughly-contacted leads from active lists to maintain focus.

named_methods.name: ABAB Cadence
named_methods.description: Day 1: Send email (List A). Day 2: Call. Day 3: Follow-up email (List A). Day 4: Call. Repeat every 2 days. Structured multi-touch avoids random timing.

named_methods.name: Cold Reading Personalization
named_methods.description: Identify prospect via public content (YouTube, LinkedIn). Observe a pattern directly. Reference pattern. Transition to offer. No bold/quoted variables. No surveillance language ('I noticed you engaged with X'). Use topic framing ('Companies in your space are seeing Y results').

named_methods.name: Micro-Commitments Ladder
named_methods.description: Provide a Give (video, insight, audit) before asking for a call. Small commitment (30-second video watch) precedes larger commitment (discovery call). Reciprocity forces conversion.

named_methods.name: Gap-Analysis Outreach
named_methods.description: Identify business deficiency (low rating, no website, missing social). Auto-generate custom audit report. Insert into email. Gate to 15-minute call. Audit report = instant perceived value; high conversion for local business segment.

named_methods.name: List Sanitation and Recycling
named_methods.description: After campaign exhaustion, filter by 'completed, no reply.' Wait 3-6 months. Re-upload with updated value proposition (different offer, new angle). Warm list with fresh angle often produces 2-3x better response than first touch.

named_methods.name: ICP + Signal + Messaging Triangle
named_methods.description: ICP definition: industries, sizes, roles, key triggers. Right lead: matches ICP, has problem you solve, can make decisions. Signal qualification: funding rounds, leadership changes, hiring patterns, product launches, tech stack. Message framework: problem statement, credibility proof (metrics/outcomes), thought leader recommendation in postscript.

prompts: Make this cold email more polarizing for [target niche]. Speak to the specific pain points of [ideal customer].
Extract target industry and investment criteria from this company website and create a 1-2 sentence personalized opening line.
Simplify this cold email to a junior-high reading level while keeping the core offer intact.
Create 5 curiosity-driven subject line variants without first-name placeholders.
Generate spin-tax for this email body: vary openers (Hi/Hey/Hello), vary CTAs, vary signatures so no two emails are identical.
Identify 3-5 high-urgency pain points for [niche] from customer complaints and industry research. Translate each to outcome language.
Write an assumptive CTA requesting a specific time: 'What does your Thursday afternoon look like?' not 'Let me know when you're free.'
Create a pre-call qualification form that filters non-ICP leads without being abrasive (revenue, deal size, specific criteria).
Write a high-value micro-offer (free audit/teardown) that removes risk and forces prospect to a 15-minute call.
Build a signal waterfall: primary filter [criteria], secondary filter [criteria], tertiary trigger [signal]. Map each to specific copy variants.
Generate a 12-step multi-channel follow-up sequence (email + call + LinkedIn) for prospects who engaged but didn't book.
Based on [contact_summary], write a one-liner about their professional experience.
Visit this website and extract: case studies, specific keywords, what they do, and recent company news for personalization.
Write a status-alignment follow-up (not a breakup email): inquire whether priorities have shifted and suggest an alternative stakeholder if needed.
[cold-copywriting] trigger pattern for Claude Skills: use explicit bracket command to force correct skill selection in Sales Brain
Instruct co-pilot: 'You are my ideal outbound assistant. My offer is [X]. My ICP is [Y]. My frameworks are [Z]. Standardize all outreach outputs using this context.'
weird_gold: Read emulation on Outlook warm-up accounts: toggle on so accounts scroll through emails during warm-up; makes accounts appear human to spam filters
PS as primary real estate: postscript is often the most-read part of an email; use it for main CTA not a secondary thought; captures skimmers
Reply-to-whitelist signal: ask for a simple 'yes' reply in first onboarding email; one reply signals high engagement to email servers; prevents Promo tab for entire list
Parenthetical humanization: light parenthetical phrases (informal, conversational breaks) defeat AI-pattern detection in spam filters; makes GPT-written copy read human
Status alignment inquiry over breakup email: replace 'just checking in' breakup follow-up with status-alignment question suggesting alternative stakeholder; feels less like harassment
Lookalike domain cloning in SuperSearch: drop best customer domain into filter; SuperSearch finds structurally similar companies
Pre-call form as time filter: Calendly gated behind mandatory qualification (revenue, deal size); auto-cancels non-ICP calls; scales gatekeeping
List recycling window: 3-6 month gap before re-contacting 'no replies'; different offer, different angle; often 2-3x better response than first touch
50-new-leads-per-day prioritization in CRM: setting that prioritizes new leads over follow-ups when both are queued; prevents reply sequence from clogging outreach volume
Infrastructure as asset: each secondary domain is a separate account with its own reputation; slow warm-up builds equity; decouples from primary brand
One lead per company toggle in SuperSearch: reach single decision-maker per org rather than saturating an org with multiple contacts
Pre-trained AI email agent: Instantly's email agent trained on the observed email dataset in the platform (implicit knowledge base)
Infrastructure mistakes during active campaigns: described as repairing a car while driving; plan infrastructure before campaigns launch not during
Timothy Wenger in Supersearch: authored 30+ industry-specific cold email prompt templates; search his name in Supersearch to access a curated prompt library

Trigify 20-25% reply rate benchmark: apply skepticism; likely survivorship bias from featured case studies; confirms directional value of signal-driven outreach but do not anchor expectations to this number

Waterfall coverage by seniority: established professionals at larger companies have multiple email sources; newer employees at small companies are harder to find; adjust enrichment expectations accordingly
contradictions_resolved: High volume (7,000+ sends/day) vs. conservative per-inbox sending (1-5/day): resolved by infrastructure decoupling; each inbox stays conservative; multiple inboxes and domains create aggregate scale

Personalization matters vs. offer is everything: both true; heavy personalization with weak offer still fails; strong offer with light personalization often outperforms; personalization is signal, not substitute for relevance
Templates are bad vs. template reuse is standard: templates as starting point are fine; relying on them as end-state fails; systems that generate unique output from templates beat templates alone
Thought leader engagement is warm vs. don't mention the thought leader: message around the topic the thought leader discusses, not the fact of their engagement; warm signal informs tone not copy
Email closes deals vs. email can't close deals: email books calls and generates leads; sales process owns the close; email's job is first 3 steps only
